events.reason: chronic productive cough, hemoptysis, weight loss

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food for 14 days

results.text: Normal oropharyngeal flora. No predominant pathogen isolated.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Parallel linear densities and ring shadows at the right lung base, in keeping with thickened, dilated bronchi. No consolidation. No cavity or mass. No pleural effusion. Left lung clear. Heart and mediastinum normal.
reports.conclusion: Tram-track and ring opacities at the right base suggesting bronchiectasis. Prior right lower lobe consolidation has cleared.

documents.title: Pulmonary Medicine consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonary Medicine
Date of service: 01/05/2026
Reason for referral: productive cough and blood-streaked sputum after pneumonia

HPI: 33-year-old woman with chronic hypertension and a right attic cholesteatoma treated surgically last March. She describes a cough that has produced sputum every day for the better part of a year: copious, thick, yellow-green and foul, heaviest on waking. Now and then there are streaks of blood. She is tired, short of breath with exertion, and has lost weight over the last several months without trying. She had a right lower lobe pneumonia in November, treated with doxycycline by her PCP, two weeks after coming home from a two-month rural volunteer placement abroad. She works with toddlers in a busy daycare. She has never had asthma, allergies or any earlier lung problem.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg twice daily; prenatal vitamin daily. NKDA.
Smoking: about 5 pack-years, stopped at 26. No alcohol.
Family history: hypertension in both parents.
Quantiferon negative last month (PCP).

Exam: vital signs normal; weight 64.8 kg. Coarse crackles over the right lung base. Digital clubbing. No wheeze. Heart regular. No lymphadenopathy.

Chest X-ray today: tram-track and ring opacities at the right base; no consolidation, cavity or mass.

Assessment: Bronchiectasis, right base, with a current exacerbation (increased purulent sputum, hemoptysis streaking). Travel history makes it important to exclude mycobacterial infection.

Plan:
1. CT chest without contrast.
2. Sputum for routine culture and acid-fast smear and culture, three early-morning samples.
3. CBC with differential; quantitative immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM).
4. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 14 days.
5. Airway clearance: oscillating PEP device twice daily, taught today by our respiratory therapist.
6. Return in about 5 weeks with spirometry.

Thank you for asking me to see her.
Pulmonary Medicine

reports.text:
Technique: non-contrast CT of the chest with thin-section reconstructions.
Lungs: cylindrical bronchiectasis of the right lower lobe with bronchial wall thickening and mucus plugging. No cavitation. No mass or suspicious nodule. The remaining lobes are clear.
Airways: central airways patent.
Mediastinum: no lymphadenopathy. Heart normal size. No pericardial effusion.
Pleura: no effusion or pneumothorax.
Upper abdomen: unremarkable.
Bones: no aggressive lesion.
reports.conclusion: Cylindrical bronchiectasis of the right lower lobe with wall thickening and mucus plugging. No cavitation, mass or lymphadenopathy. Other lobes clear.

reports.text: Acceptable and repeatable efforts. FEV1 2.71 L (84% predicted). FVC 3.30 L (91% predicted). FEV1/FVC 0.82. Flow-volume loop normal in shape.

documents.title: Pulmonary Medicine follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonary Medicine
Date of service: 02/11/2026

Ms. Lavoie finished the 14 days of amoxicillin-clavulanate. Sputum is down to a fraction of what it was, and there has been no blood since the middle of January. Her energy is better and her weight has held steady. She is doing the oscillating PEP device twice a day.

Results: CT chest - cylindrical bronchiectasis of the right lower lobe with wall thickening and mucus plugging, no cavitation or mass, other lobes clear. Sputum - normal flora; acid-fast smears negative on all three samples, cultures pending. CBC normal. IgG 1,040, IgA 212, IgM 118 mg/dL, all normal.

Spirometry today: FEV1 2.71 L (84%), FVC 3.30 L (91%), ratio 0.82 - no obstruction.

Assessment: Right lower lobe bronchiectasis, likely post-infectious; no other cause identified on this initial evaluation. Exacerbation resolved.

Plan: continue airway clearance daily, more often during colds. Please give her a pneumococcal vaccine. Call us early for increased sputum or blood. Return in 3 months.
Pulmonary Medicine

documents.title: Office Visit - follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the lung workup.

Pulmonology letters (1/5, 2/11), CT chest and labs reviewed with her: right lower lobe bronchiectasis, felt to be post-infectious. TB evaluation negative throughout - Quantiferon negative in December, three AFB smears negative, AFB cultures final no growth on 2/20. Immunoglobulins normal. Spirometry normal.

She feels much better. A little sputum most mornings, cleared with the PEP device, which she does before work and at bedtime. No blood since mid-January. No fever. Weight 64.6, about where it was at pulmonology - no further loss.

Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP at goal. Vitals as charted. Lungs - a few crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart regular. R ear dry.

A/P
1. Bronchiectasis, RLL - on the problem list; pulmonology following, next visit May. Airway clearance daily. PCV20 today per pulmonology; flu and COVID done in December.
2. Weight loss - stable since January; recheck at next visit.
3. Cholesteatoma s/p R tympanomastoidectomy 3/2025 - ENT MRI due this spring.
4. Chronic HTN - controlled on labetalol 200 BID. Refills sent.
5. HM - Pap/HPV due this year.

RTC for physical in the summer.

reports.study: MRI internal auditory canals without contrast
reports.text:
Protocol: temporal bone imaging with non-echo-planar diffusion-weighted sequences, coronal T1 and T2. History: right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma 03/2025.
No restricted diffusion in the right middle ear or mastoid. Postoperative changes of the right mastoid. Left temporal bone normal. Internal auditory canals and cerebellopontine angles normal. Visualized brain unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of residual or recurrent right cholesteatoma.

documents.title: Otolaryngology surveillance visit
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside Otolaryngology
Date of service: 04/08/2026

One year after right canal-wall-up tympanomastoidectomy for attic cholesteatoma. The ear has stayed dry. Exam: healed graft, no retraction, canal clean. Diffusion-weighted MRI 04/06: no restricted diffusion, no residual or recurrent disease.

Medications: labetalol, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Plan: yearly ear checks with us. Return sooner for drainage.
Otolaryngology

documents.title: Pulmonary Medicine follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside Pulmonary Medicine
Date of service: 05/20/2026

Three-month follow-up for right lower lobe bronchiectasis. Small amount of sputum in the mornings only, no blood, no exacerbation since January. Final acid-fast cultures were negative. Received pneumococcal vaccine in February.

Lungs: scattered crackles right base, otherwise clear. Oxygen saturation normal.

Plan: continue daily airway clearance with the PEP device. Early contact for any flare. Follow-up in 6 months.
Pulmonary Medicine
